title: Stacks
summary: Use a stack like a pile of plates. Push two items, pop the newest one, and check for an empty stack before looking at its top.
introduction: When you stack plates, the last plate you put down is the first one you lift. A stack gives programs the same rule. It helps with undo buttons and keeping track of unfinished jobs.
learningObjectives: Push, pop, and peek at a small stack
Guard an empty stack and a full fixed-size stack

blocks.text: A **stack** lets us add or remove an item at one end, called the top. **Push** adds an item. **Pop** removes and returns the top item. **Peek** reads the top without removing it.
The rule is **last in, first out**, often shortened to LIFO. An undo list uses this idea: undo the newest action before an older action.
A stack is a rule for using data. It can be built with an array or linked nodes. Library stacks hide those storage details. In the C example, size tells us how many array places are in use.

items: Push 10, then push 20. The top is now 20.
Check the stack is not empty. Pop and print 20.
Check again. Peek and print 10, leaving it on the stack.

blocks.text: Choose one tab. All six programs do the same task and print the same result. JavaScript can run here. The other languages need the separate local tools in [Language setup](/tutorials/data-structures-algorithms/language-setup).

stack.append(20)

blocks.text: The newest item, 20, leaves first. Peeking then shows 10. C++ separates reading the top from removing it because its pop method does not return the removed value.
Check the small and tricky cases
An empty stack has nothing to pop or peek. The checks keep the examples safe. In the C example, pushing also checks size < 3 because the array has room for only three items.
These top operations usually take O(1) work. A growing array may occasionally need to copy its items into more space. Over many pushes, such growth is spread out across the pushes.

items: Push 30 after pushing 20 and before the pop. In C, use the same size < 3 check.
The output becomes 30 then 20. Item 10 is still at the bottom. Pop order follows the order of pushes in reverse.

blocks.title: A common mistake
blocks.text: Do not remove from the first array position when you mean a stack top at the end. That changes which item leaves and may require shifting items.
